headline: Electric school runs, petrol backup
summary: A practical used PHEV to inspect if you can charge at home. This Aspire has five seats; seven-seat Exceed versions are different configurations. The published three-across test was a later five-seat ZM, so your restraint trial remains essential.

range.basis: Electric only · ADR 81/02 / NEDC claim; not WLTP

battery.basis: Manufacturer-rated pack capacity; usable capacity not confirmed

consumption.basis: Not independently verified for this configuration

depletedConsumption.basis: Charge-depleted petrol consumption unverified; weighted PHEV fuel figures are not substituted

chargeTime: Australian MY 24 brochure: approximately 6.5 h with a suitable 15 A AC EVSE, 9.5 h on 240V/10 A, or 38min DC to 80%; battery temperature, initial charge and charger conditions affect times. AC/DC peak power is not stated in this brochure.
connector: Type 2 AC / CHAdeMO DC; confirm charger availability on your routes.

boot.basis: VDA · five seats upright, to top of second-row seatback

towing.basis: Maximum braked trailer capacity; loading and towbar limits apply

warranty: Up to 10 years / 200,000 km when eligible scheduled services are completed at Mitsubishi; confirm this used car’s eligibility.
batteryWarranty: 8 years / 160,000 km. MY 22 onward Capacity Care program has a 66% usable-capacity threshold, subject to terms.
servicing: MY 23 capped-price schedule is linked; confirm the VIN schedule and dealer-service eligibility before purchase.

safety.applicability: Original ZM petrol/PHEV specification. PHEV built from July 2025 has a separate 2025 assessment; inspect build date.

familyFit.summary: Three across reported in an April 2025 test of a five-seat 20 kWh ES. Aspire shares the ZM cabin, but the tested grade and your exact restraints differ.
familyFit.row2: Two outboard ISOFIX pairs; three top tethers. Centre tether is overhead above the boot.
familyFit.row3: This Aspire has no third row. Seven-seat ZM models lack third-row top tethers.
familyFit.testedSeats: April 2025 BabyDrive five-seat ES 20 kWh test fitted three restraints, including a rear-facing infant capsule. Article text does not identify every restraint make/model; this is not an exact Aspire test.
familyFit.buckleAccess: No repeatable booster-buckle clearance measurement published; test your combination.
familyFit.access: Check rear-door loading with every restraint fitted and front seats set for both adults.
familyFit.ventilation: MY 24 Aspire brochure explicitly lists rear centre-console air vents; no third row.

pros: Published three-across evidence for the five-seat ZM cabin.
Plug-in driving for daily local trips with petrol backup.
Useful boot with no third row taking up space.
cons: CHAdeMO public charging needs route checking.
Five-seat Aspire provides no extra row.
Verified electric-distance consumption and charge-depleted fuel use remain unavailable; calculator proxies are separately labelled.
inspection: Check the VIN against current official recall campaigns; this dataset is not a complete recall history.
Ask for proof that applicable rear-view camera software recall REC-005692 was completed.
Request a battery health report and demonstrate charging from your planned AC equipment.
Identify the 20 kWh specification from build/VIN, rather than registration year alone.
Australian MY 24 brochure specifies unleaded, minimum 91 RON recommended; select the matching fuel grade when editing petrol-cost assumptions.

changes.text: 20 kWh ZM PHEV. Verified MY 24 brochure separates five-seat Aspire from seven-seat Exceed; exact annual equipment needs the period order sheet.
Larger-battery version is a separate entry. Mitsubishi’s brochure is labelled MY 25, so verify the actual build specification.

gaps: 2021 ZL predecessor is not profiled; do not apply these ZM dimensions or fit evidence to it.
AC/DC peak power and charge-depleted petrol/electric consumption are not verified in the Australian brochure. The 1.5 L/100 km weighted claim cannot support a depleted-battery estimate.
Seven-seat 20 kWh Exceed and trim-specific equipment need a separate listing-level check.

headline: An EV-like drive without a charging plug

batteryWarranty: Pre-MY 27 HV battery capacity warranty: 7 years / 150,000 km with a 70% threshold, subject to the applicable terms.
servicing: Obtain a VIN-specific service schedule and confirm completed logbook services.

safety.applicability: ANCAP extends the 2020 MQ 4 rating to HEV/PHEV variants; listed expiry December 2026. Rating year differs from vehicle year.

familyFit.summary: 2025 GT-Line test demonstrated restraints across both rear rows; MY 26 fit pending.
familyFit.row2: Tested GT-Line: two outboard ISOFIX pairs, three seatback top tethers.
familyFit.row3: ISOFIX and top tethers on both third-row seats; current brochure lists five top tethers and four ISOFIX positions overall. Curtain airbags cover the first and second rows only.
familyFit.testedSeats: 2025 article demonstrates three restraints in row two and two in row three; exact brand/model combination not fully stated in text. 2021 PHEV test is linked separately.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Check every booster buckle with the proposed two-plus-one arrangement; no quantified clearance is published.
familyFit.access: 2025 test required removing one restraint for access with three across. With two fitted, an ISOFIX-mounted seat could move; verify manual/tether instructions.
familyFit.ventilation: Tested GT-Line has row-two console vents and row-three side vents with fan control.

pros: Published third-row ISOFIX and top-tether positions.
Multiple ways to arrange three child seats.
Rear ventilation in both rows on the tested GT-Line.
cons: Small boot with all rows upright.
Three across can block everyday third-row access.
Australian MY 26 brochure lists curtain airbags for the first and second rows, not the third.
inspection: Check the VIN against current official recall campaigns; this dataset is not a complete recall history.
Check third-row restraint and curtain-airbag coverage in the Australian manual and ANCAP technical report.
Test a two-in-row-two plus one-in-row-three arrangement, including adult loading access.
Confirm MY 26 versus earlier facelift specifications; older AWD fuel figures differ.
Kia Australia states Sorento HEV uses regular 91-octane petrol, E 10 compatible; do not apply current PHEV premium-fuel guidance to this HEV.

changes.text: Facelift GT-Line family test and current MY 26 mechanical figures are separate sources. Current AWD combined claim is 5.7 L/100 km.

gaps: Earlier 2022–2025 HEV variants are not fully profiled; do not assign MY 26 figures or equipment to them.
Live availability, final drive-away price and VIN-specific service eligibility require confirmation.

headline: The strongest documented seat flexibility here
summary: The original Australian PHEV has a specific five-restraint family test, 68 km WLTP electric range and 3.3 kW single-phase charging. Its 1350 kg braked towing and 175 L boot with seven seats differ from the HEV and later facelift.

range.basis: Electric only · WLTP, Australian MY 23 manufacturer sheet; not NEDC or total petrol+electric range.

battery.basis: Australian MY 23 sheet rounds battery energy to 14 kWh; nominal advertised 13.8 kWh is not substituted from overseas specifications. Not usable energy.

consumption.basis: Published WLTP energy consumption 161 Wh/km converted to 16.1 kWh/100 km. Sheet does not state weighting or charging boundary; not verified electric-distance consumption for automatic costs.

depletedConsumption.basis: Charge-depleted petrol consumption unverified; weighted PHEV fuel figures are not substituted

acCharging.basis: Maximum onboard AC charging · single phase, Australian MY 23 sheet.

dcCharging.basis: AC-only Type 2 charging inlet listed in the Australian MY 23 sheet; DC charging is not provided.

chargeTime: Australian MY 23 brochure:15–95% in 3 h 25min using a suitable 3.3 kW single-phase AC EVSE; temperature, initial charge and equipment affect time. This is not a 0–100% claim.
connector: Type 2 AC only · no DC rapid charging.

boot.basis: VDA · second row upright and third row folded; original Australian PHEV, not 608L HEV.

bootAllRows.basis: VDA · all seven seats upright; original PHEV, not 179L HEV.

length.basis: Overall body length · original MQ 4; later facelift 4815 mm is separate.

towing.basis: Maximum braked towing · original Australian MY 23 PHEV. Later MY 26 PHEV 1010 kg must not be substituted.

warranty: 7 years / unlimited km for ordinary private use; remaining cover depends on original delivery and applicable terms.
batteryWarranty: Pre-MY 27 HV battery capacity terms list 7 years / 150,000 km and a 70% threshold; confirm the original vehicle booklet.
servicing: Obtain a VIN-specific service schedule and confirm completed logbook services.

safety.applicability: ANCAP 2020 MQ 4 rating applies to Australian PHEV variants; it is not a 2021 or 2023 test.

familyFit.summary: 2021 PHEV test fitted three restraints in row two and two boosters in row three.
familyFit.row2: Two outboard ISOFIX pairs and top tethers across all three seats.
familyFit.row3: Both third-row seats have ISOFIX and top tethers in the Australian ANCAP report. The report lists side-head airbags for the first and second rows only.
familyFit.testedSeats: Row two: two InfaSecure Attain More plus an Achieve More, tried forward/rear-facing. Row three: Aspire More and Roamer II boosters, forward-facing.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Check independent buckle reach using your particular boosters and neighbouring restraints.
familyFit.access: 2021 test found ISOFIX installations could allow bench movement. A later HEV test differed with three across; verify the exact arrangement and manual.
familyFit.ventilation: Original AustralianMY 23 brochure and 2021 test both confirm row-two console vents and row-three vents/fan control.

pros: Specific Australian restraint combinations documented.
Both rear rows offer top tethers and ISOFIX positions.
Can combine home charging with petrol backup.
cons: Only 175L VDA boot space with all seven seats occupied.
ANCAP/manufacturer list side-head airbags for the first and second rows; third-row coverage is absent.
Slow 3.3 kW AC-only charging; no DC option.
Verified charge-depleted petrol consumption remains unavailable; weighted 1.6 L/100 km is not a depleted-battery rate.
inspection: Check the VIN against current official recall campaigns; this dataset is not a complete recall history.
Verify the build-year Australian PHEV brochure and charging hardware before comparing powertrain numbers.
Check third-row curtain-airbag coverage and restraint compatibility in the manual.
Demonstrate charging and request service/battery-health records.

Fuel guidance conflicts by period: MY 23 Australian brochure says Regular Unleaded, while current Kia Australia guidance says Sorento PHEV requires 95 RON. Use 95 for a conservative budget until the exact original car’s filler flap/manual is verified.

changes.text: Published Australian 2021 family test and a 2022 used listing identify the original MQ 4 PHEV. Later facelift equipment is not assumed.
Current manufacturer brochure has a broader grade range and different body specification; use a separate configuration for that model.

gaps: Australian period sheet publishes 16.1 kWh/100 km WLTP energy consumption but does not identify weighted-versus-electric-distance or charging boundary. Verified combined-cost calculation still needs that distinction.
No verified charge-depleted petrol figure; weighted 1.6 L/100 km is excluded from that role.
MY 23 sheet verifies the original MQ 4 mechanical figures; exact 2021/2022 annual equipment and buyer-specific warranty eligibility still require the period order sheet/manual.
Later 2024–2026 PHEV variants remain outside this original configuration.

Original MY 23 Regular Unleaded wording conflicts with current Kia PHEV 95 RON guidance; confirm the period VIN manual/fuel flap. A premium-rate budget is conservative, not a resolved original specification.
